text: John Bennett? Do you remember me?
Of course! We met at university, didn't we?
That's right. What are you doing these days?
I'm working for a technology company in Manchester.
Really? What do you do there?
I'm a project analyst. I usually work with different teams, but this week I'm helping the sales department.
That sounds interesting.
Mary, this is Rick. Rick, this is Mary Collins.
Nice to meet you, Rick. What do you do?
I'm a photographer. I work for a local newspaper.
Do you take photographs of sport?
Yes, I do. I'm the sports photographer, so I often cover football matches.
Mary works in our company. She's a software engineer.
And John is being modest. He's very good at solving problems.
Do you still live near the city centre?
No, I live in a suburb outside Manchester.
How long have you lived there?
I've lived there for three years. It's quiet, and the neighbours are friendly.
Are you still taking photographs?
Yes. I usually take pictures at weekends. At the moment, I'm working on a small photography project.
This is a photograph of my family.
Is that your sister?
Yes. Her name is Ana Mitchell. She's a teacher.
And the man next to her?
That's my uncle, Stuart Hughes. He's an engineer.
What do you do in your free time?
I enjoy photography, I play football with Peter, and I sometimes go swimming.
I play squash every Saturday morning. You should come along sometime.
I'd like that.
Look! Peter is waiting for us outside.
Is he standing by the main entrance?
Yes, and Rick is talking to him.
Let's go and say hello.
They're waving at us now.
John, this is Ruan Parker. He organises events around the city.
Nice to meet you. Rick has told me a lot about you.
Nice to meet you too.
And this is my colleague, Ketlyn Brooks.
Hello, everyone. Are you all coming to the family lunch on Sunday?
Yes. My cousin Joana Fletcher is coming as well.
It sounds like a big gathering!
It will be. My family usually gets together at weekends.
What are you studying at the moment?
I'm studying Business and Commerce at the University of Manchester.
Are you studying full-time?
No. I work during the day and study in the evenings.
Perhaps we can meet at the university sometime.
I'd like that.
What does the greengrocer do?
He sells vegetables. And the electrician is fixing a light over there.
The singer is performing now, but she usually works in a theatre.
When did you last see Peter?
I met him last week at a conference.
Was he going out with anyone at the time?
I don't know. He's married now.
Do you usually arrive at the office before nine, John?
Yes, I do. I usually get here at half past eight.
What do you do first?
I check my emails, read the project notes and speak to my team.
Are you working on the new system today?
Yes. I'm checking the figures because the sales team needs the report this afternoon.
I see. I'm preparing the presentation at the moment.
This is Mary Collins. She's a software engineer.
What does she do exactly?
She designs and tests computer programmes.
And John analyses the projects and helps the teams organise their work.
Who looks after the office equipment?
Peter does. He's an electrician, and he repairs electrical appliances.
Are you still studying in the evenings?
Yes. I'm taking an online course in project management.
How often do you have classes?
Twice a week. I usually study on Tuesdays and Thursdays.
Does it take a lot of time?
It does, but I've learnt a lot so far.
That's great. Keep going!
John, are you free for a moment?
I'm afraid not. I'm dealing with a problem in the new system.
Has the team found the cause?
Not yet. We've checked the files, but we haven't found the error.
I can help. I know this part of the system.
Thanks. That would be very helpful.
Are you going straight home, John?
Not today. I'm meeting Rick and Jessy at the sports centre.
Do you play football there?
Sometimes. Today we're going swimming.
I haven't been swimming for ages.
Come with us, then!
I usually travel by train, but I sometimes drive to work.
I'm going to visit my aunt this weekend.
My nephew Rodri is younger than Penelope, but he isn't the youngest person in the family.
Mary, this is my sister, Ana Mitchell.
Nice to meet you, Ana.
Nice to meet you too. Are you John's colleague?
Yes. We work together.
And this is my uncle, Stuart Hughes. He's my mother's brother.
Hello, Mary. Please, sit down.
Thank you. What a lovely family!
Is Stuart your oldest uncle, John?
No. He's younger than my uncle Peter, but he's older than my father.
How old is your sister?
Ana is twenty-eight. I'm thirty-two.
So you're older than Ana.
That's right, but she's the tallest person in our family!
Who is the little girl in this photograph?
She's my niece, Penelope Clarke. She's my sister's daughter.
And the boy next to her?
That's my nephew, Rodri Morgan. He's my brother's son.
Do they live nearby?
Yes. Their grandparents live in the same town.
Who's that man in the photograph with Rick?
That's Peter Walker. He's one of Rick's oldest friends.
Is he the most talkative one?
Definitely! He's probably the funniest person in the group.
I think Rick is funnier.
Maybe a little, but Peter is more outgoing than Rick.
Which one do you prefer spending time with?
I like them both. They're different, but they're both great friends.
What do you think of the new café?
I think it's nicer than the old one.
Really? I don't think it's as good as the café near the station.
Which one do you prefer, then?
I prefer the one near the station. Their coffee is the best.
What do you think of Rick's new photograph?
It's nicer than the last one, but Mary's is the most impressive.
Which one do you prefer?
I think Mary's is the nicest.
Ruan is getting married next week. His friends are organising a stag do.
And his future wife is having a hen do with her friends.
They are going to a nightclub afterwards.
What shall we do on Saturday?
We could go to the football match.
Again? Have you got any better ideas?
There's a sports event in the park. We could watch the race.
That's a good idea. What time does it start?
It starts at half past ten.
Look! The runner in the blue shirt is in first place.
He's closely followed by the runner in red.
The runner in green is coming up quickly.
He's taken up second position!
And the runner in red has gone back to third.
What a finish! The blue runner comes in first.
That was great fun!
The runner in blue was brilliant.
He must train every day.
Perhaps. But the runner in green kept trying until the end.
That's what matters. You must keep trying.
Shall we get something to eat?
Yes. I'm starving!
Where shall we go?
There's a new restaurant in King Street.
Is it better than the one near the station?
I haven't tried it yet, but people say it's very good.
Let's give it a try.
Good idea. We can talk about the race over lunch.
Are you doing anything next Saturday, Jessy?
Not that I know of. Why?
We're having a small get-together at my place. Would you like to come?
I'd love to. What time?
Around seven. I'll send you the address.
Lovely. See you then!
Number seven gets a good start and takes first position, closely followed by number four in second place.
Number one moves up into third place, while number three drops back to fifth.
Number seven has won the race! Number one is second, and number four comes in third.
Mr Walker is on the phone for you, Mary.
Thank you. Could you put him through, please?
Certainly.
Hello, Mr Walker. How are you today?
Very well, thank you. I'm hoping you could advise me on a new computer system.
Of course. What would you like to know?
Which of your products would most suit a small business?
I can explain the options. Could you meet me later this afternoon?
Yes. I'm free at about half past five. Is that all right with you?
That's fine. How about the Palace Hotel? They have a wonderful restaurant.
That sounds good. I'll see you there at half five, then.
Mary, are you available tomorrow morning?
It depends. What time are you thinking of?
Could we meet at nine?
I'm afraid I can't make it at nine. Could we meet at half past nine instead?
That would suit me.
Shall I book a meeting room?
Yes, please. Thanks for arranging it.
Where can we go next Friday?
We could go to the cinema.
The cinema again? Have you got any better ideas?
There's a new club that has just opened in Duke Street.
Where's that?
Near the old library. How about meeting there at half past eight?
That sounds good. I'll see you there.
Are we still meeting at the Palace Hotel?
Yes. I've booked a table for six people.
What time should we arrive?
At about half past five.
Perfect. I'll be there a little early.
You need something smart for the meeting.
I know. I haven't bought a suit for years.
There's a good clothes shop in the city centre.
Shall we have a look this afternoon?
Certainly. I can help you choose.
Good afternoon. Can I help you?
Yes, please. I'm looking for a suit for a business meeting.
What size are you?
I'm not sure. Could I try this one on?
Of course. The changing rooms are over here.
This jacket is a little too large. Have you got a smaller size?
I'll have a look for you.
That colour suits you.
Do you think so? I'll try the shirt as well.
Excuse me. Could you show me a blue shirt, please?
Certainly. What size would you like?
A medium, if you have one.
Here you are. Would you like to try it on?
Yes, please. Where can I change?
The changing rooms are over here.
Thank you.
How about this dark blue suit?
I like it, but the grey one is cheaper.
The blue one looks smarter, though.
You're right. I think I'll take it.
Would you like anything else?
No, thank you. Just the suit and the shirt.
Have you got everything for the meeting?
Almost. I've bought a suit and a shirt.
Have you tried them on?
Yes. They fit perfectly.
Great. You'll look very smart.
Have you booked your train ticket yet?
Not yet. I'm checking the times now.
There are several trains in the morning.
I'd like to get there before eleven.
You could take the 8.20 train.
That would be ideal. How long does the journey take?
About two and a half hours.
Excuse me. Could you tell me how to get to the railway station?
Certainly. Go straight on and turn left at the traffic lights.
Is it far from here?
No, it's about ten minutes on foot.
Thank you very much.
Where can I find the departure board?
It's just over there, next to platform three.
Could you tell me which platform the Edinburgh train leaves from?
Platform five. It leaves at twenty past eight.
Thank you. Is the train direct?
Yes, it is.
The 8.20 service to Edinburgh is delayed by ten minutes. We apologise for the inconvenience.
Oh, no. Is it always late?
What's happened?
The train is delayed. They're saying it'll be another ten minutes.
That's inconvenient. Have you asked the staff?
Not yet. I'll speak to someone at the information desk.
Excuse me. Is there another train to Edinburgh?
There's one at 9.05, but it stops at several stations.
Would I still arrive before eleven?
I'm afraid not. You'd arrive at about half past eleven.
I see. I'll wait for the direct service, then.
It should be here shortly.
Good morning. How can I help you?
I'd like to book a flight to Boston, please.
Certainly. When would you like to travel?
Next Thursday, if possible. Have you got any early flights?
We have a flight at around nine o'clock. There are also several charter flights later in the day.
The early flight would suit me better.
Would you like me to book it?
Yes, please.
Have you checked in online?
Yes. I only need to drop off my suitcase.
What time do you board?
At eight twenty. I should get to the gate by eight.
Don't forget to pick up your passport.
It's in my bag. Thanks for reminding me.
Could you tell me how much further it is to the station?
It isn't much further. Keep walking until you see the bus stop.
I'd like to make a complaint about the service. The train is two hours late.
I'm sorry. I'll check the timetable and explain the delay.
